title: The Part Sale side prices only Part Sales
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts', 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit' and 'Part Sales — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new matrix for this test, matrix A, pricing a new category made for this test, category A, Default 50% markup on both sides, Separate Part Sale pricing on.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, on Default.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, with one labor line (line 1).
  • Have a new Part Sale for this test, Part Sale 1, for customer A.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Matrices tab on Settings › Pricing.
  2. Click matrix A's name on the Matrices list.
  3. Click the Part Sale Matrix tab.
  4. Click Edit.
  5. Type 20 in Default's first range.
  6. Click Save.
  7. Open work order 1.
  8. Click Add Part under line 1.
  9. Type a description in Description (for example Test part).
  10. Type 1 in Qty.
  11. Pick category A in Category.
  12. Type 100.00 in Cost.
  13. Click Save.
  14. Open Part Sale 1.
  15. Add a part with a cost of $100.00 in category A.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Matrix A is listed.

Step 2:

  • Matrix A's page opens.

Step 3:

  • The Part Sale grid shows.

Step 4:

  • The Part Sale grid is in edit.

Step 5:

  • Default's first range reads 20.

Step 6:

  • The Part Sale grid saves.

Step 7:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 8:

  • A new part row opens under line 1 with Part number, Description, Qty, Category, Cost and Sell price boxes and Save and Cancel.

Step 9:

  • Description holds the typed text.

Step 10:

  • Qty holds 1.

Step 11:

  • Category shows category A.

Step 12:

  • Cost holds 100.00 as typed.

Step 13:

  • The work order line is priced by the Work Order Matrix: $100.00 × 1.50 = $150.00.

Step 14:

  • Part Sale 1 opens.

Step 15:

  • The Part Sale line is priced by the Part Sale side: $100.00 × 1.20 = $120.00.
